title: Simile and metaphor practice sheet
subject: English
unit: Summer 2: Time Traveller and Off with Her Head!
source: Written for english/y5 lesson 83 (Simile and metaphor practice sheet (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 83: Similes and metaphors for character. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

head: Simile
Metaphor
rows: She was as calm as a still pond.
She was a still pond in a storm.

parts.text: Find something brave and steady: a lighthouse
Extend: She was a lighthouse in the dark, guiding the others home.

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: She was a lighthouse in the dark, guiding the others home.

head: Not this
This
rows: His temper was a feather and a volcano.
His temper was a volcano: quiet for years, then sudden and fierce.

keywords.def: a comparison using like or as
saying something IS something else to compare it
what a word makes the reader think or feel
bright and clear in the mind

questions.q: Write a simile for a time traveller's coat
questions.a: For example: as dusty as an old attic

questions.q: Turn into a metaphor: He was like a fox.
Core: write three similes for appearance and two metaphors for personality
Extend: explain the effect of your best metaphor in two sentences
questions.a: For example: Calling her a compass suggests she always knows the right direction. It shows she is wise and calm.

questions.q: Stretch: extend a metaphor across two sentences
questions.a: For example: He was a clock. He ticked through each day, never late, never rushing.

questions.q: 'Her laugh was sunshine.' What does it suggest?
options: she makes people feel warm and happy
questions.a: B) she makes people feel warm and happy. Sunshine brings warmth and brightness, so her laugh cheers people.
